description: A beast crowned with one great amethyst horn. It headbutts like a landslide and grazes on buried gems.
lore: Amethyrn never fell and never was anyone. Count instead the men who went into a hill certain — properly certain, the way you are certain of your own hand — that the next foot of rock had something in it, and count how many of them were wrong. Then work out what a few thousand years of that settles into, given nowhere to be and nothing else to do. It got up. It is the size of a cart, plated like a woodlouse, and it is never wrong.

The horn is one piece of amethyst as long as your forearm, and it is not the useful part. What the beast grazes comes back up through its shoulders in clusters, so a bull that has been feeding well is wearing the assay on its own back, and a patient man with a glass can read a whole hill from the next ridge. That is why people follow it. It headbutts like a landslide. That is why they follow it from the next ridge.

[[characters/54bead23|Osric]] has spent two years trying to reach a seam before it does and has not managed it once, which he considers unreasonable in a thing that walks slower than he does. He arrived recently enough to still count his age in living years. He is saving — in [[lore/the_gold_agreement|gold]], the one substance here that does not drift — and has not yet worked out what for. [[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] pointed out, kindly, over a fire, that Osric has all the time there is. Osric said that was the worry.
gm_notes: Shipped description adopted verbatim — accurate to the art (low armoured quadruped, ridged plates, one huge amethyst nose-horn, amethyst clusters at both shoulders, violet eyes) and better than anything I had. This is the batch's Made record and its comic one: a creature that is nothing but prospectors' certainty, which is right every time none of them were. The shoulder-clusters are the mechanic worth keeping — you read the beast, not the ground. Osric is the sting: a newly woken man still running a living man's arithmetic, racing a thing he has eternity to beat. Also the first entity record to wire in the_gold_agreement, which was the least-referenced chapter in the set. NO loot is bound to this creature; it eats gems and that is all anyone knows about what it leaves.
